meta.note: First messages of the regular session (from 09:30:00). The whole day before the window was replayed through the true book, so the book is the real one at the open. Decisions: golden strategy_imbalance -> risk_check chain (position limit 250), trading enabled at 09:30. Message side/price for E/X/D/C are the resting order's; wire_bytes = ITCH message + 2-byte MoldUDP64 length. Prices in 1e-4 USD.

pipeline.label: SFP+ in
pipeline.desc: 10GBASE-R optical/DAC link into the K26 GTH transceiver (bank 224). Not simulated.

pipeline.label: PCS/PMA rx
pipeline.desc: 64b/66b decode, gearbox, elastic buffer -> 64-bit XGMII at 156.25 MHz. AMD IP; latency not measured here.

pipeline.label: RX class filter
pipeline.desc: One shared port: feed path keeps UDP, order path keeps TCP+ARP. Pass-through, zero added cycles; a rejected frame is cut at beat 1-2 and dropped.

pipeline.label: 10G MAC rx
pipeline.desc: Strips preamble/FCS, checks FCS, lane-4 start realign; first byte out ~3 XGMII words (19 ns, xgmii_mac_rx.sv header). Line rate, no back-pressure.

pipeline.label: Feed packet FIFO (CDC)
pipeline.desc: XGMII 156.25 MHz -> core 250 MHz crossing, whole frames only; bad or overflowing frames dropped whole and counted. Crossing latency not separately measured.

pipeline.label: 64->8 unpack
pipeline.desc: 64-bit beats -> 1 byte per 250 MHz cycle: the 2 Gb/s core-side limit.

pipeline.label: UDP rx
pipeline.desc: Ethernet/IPv4/UDP header checks, dst IP+port match; payload out cut-through (zero added latency, udp_rx.sv header). UDP checksum deliberately not checked.

pipeline.label: MoldUDP64 A/B
pipeline.desc: Sequence-aware A/B arbitration, dedup, gap -> feed_halt. One line (A) on the KR260 build.

pipeline.label: ITCH parser
pipeline.desc: ITCH 5.0 A/F/X/D/E/C/U/P/S/H/Y/Q -> structured message pulse. Counted inside the 70 ns t2t.

pipeline.label: Symbol KVS
pipeline.desc: stock_locate -> book slot (fixes the low-bits aliasing). Counted inside the 70 ns t2t.

pipeline.label: Order book v3
pipeline.desc: Exact order-by-order book: 2-choice hash store (196,608 orders in 48 URAM on the KR260 build, 64k default) + per-side ±$327 ladder bitmaps + 8k level tables. Add ready for the next message after 5 cycles (20 ns), C/D/E 18 cycles, U 22 (full-day replay cycle counts). Counted inside the 70 ns t2t.

pipeline.label: Strategy engine
pipeline.desc: Decision out. 70 ns = first ITCH byte into the parser -> decision_valid (latency_counter, tb_tick_to_trade with order_book_v3; 65 ns with BOOK_FAST_DIV=1, m2 book 55 ns).

pipeline.label: Pre-trade risk
pipeline.desc: SEC 15c3-5 gate: size, price band, position, rate, halt. Combinational: zero added latency (risk_check.sv header).

pipeline.label: OUCH encoder
pipeline.desc: OUCH 4.2 Enter Order in a SoupBinTCP 'U' packet, 52 bytes. On real AAPL the first OUCH byte left 9 cycles (36 ns) after the last ITCH byte and the whole order by cycle 15 (60 ns; multi_symbol_top sim, m2 book).

pipeline.label: SoupBinTCP session
pipeline.desc: Login, sequence numbers, heartbeats; no orders unless logged in.

pipeline.label: TCP client
pipeline.desc: One TCP connection, message per segment, retransmit/fast-retransmit. Store-and-forward per message: 36 ns of OUCH + TCP buffering on the 8-byte order path, 52 cycles at 1 byte/cycle.

pipeline.label: 8->64 pack
pipeline.desc: Bytes -> 64-bit beats with tkeep. Bypassed on the KR260 build (ORDER_TX_BYTES=8).

pipeline.label: TX packet FIFO (CDC)
pipeline.desc: Core -> XGMII crossing; the MAC cannot pause mid-frame, so whole frames only.

pipeline.label: 10G MAC tx
pipeline.desc: Adds preamble/SFD, FCS, IPG; ARP replies inserted between frames by arp_responder.

pipeline.label: PCS/PMA tx
pipeline.desc: 64b/66b encode + serializer. AMD IP; latency not measured here.

pipeline.label: SFP+ out
pipeline.desc: To the exchange gateway.

pipeline.label: Host (ARM PS)
pipeline.desc: Zynq PS on AXI-Lite: symbol table, session config, halt/strategy select/heartbeat, decisions + exchange replies + statistics read back through CDC FIFOs.

chokepoints.label: 8-bit core side vs 10G line
chokepoints.peak_note: This window's busiest 10 µs of AAPL-only ITCH: 2.765 Gb/s (the 09:30 opening cross) -- above the 2 Gb/s core side for that instant, absorbed by the 32 KB feed FIFO. Whole-market ITCH on 10-18-2019 peaks at 0.9 Gb/s over 100 µs; the line itself is 10 Gb/s, so a sustained 10G burst toward the core drops whole frames at the packet FIFO.

chokepoints.label: Feed packet FIFO
chokepoints.peak_note: Worst measured whole-market 10-µs burst 12.8 KB (07-30-2019; 9.9 KB 10-18, 8.8 KB 10-30). 20 KB line-rate burst test: 0 drops; the old 4 KB FIFO dropped 8 frames.

chokepoints.label: Order-port RX FIFO on the shared SFP+
chokepoints.peak_note: Peak = frames dropped with eth_rx_filter (20 KB feed burst + 9 ARP, session up): 0. Without the filter the same burst dropped 16 frames here (negative control).

chokepoints.label: Order store (live orders, KR260 build)
chokepoints.peak_note: 08-13-2021: true peak 112,635 live orders = 57% of the K26 store (196,608 in 48 URAM), well under the ~85% d-left onset; full-day RTL replay exact, 0 faults. On the old 65,536 store the same day overflowed first at msg 83,003 and raised book_fault. 2019 days peak at 42,774 (01-30-2019).

chokepoints.label: Price-level table (per side)
chokepoints.peak_note: 08-13-2021: 5,520 bid / 2,445 ask levels, 0 overflows (2019 days peak 3,138). This window: 524 levels on one side.

chokepoints.label: Ladder window (±$327.68)
chokepoints.peak_note: Bitmap covers 65,536 pennies around a base; orders outside are tracked as 'far'. End of this window: 3 of 865 live levels lie beyond ±$327.68 of the mid (stub quotes; the full book spans $199,999.98). Top-of-book stays exact.

chokepoints.label: Decision FIFO to host
chokepoints.peak_note: Depth 32 (DEC_DEPTH). Peak = most risk-accepted decisions within any 10 µs of this window (3); 108 of 901 strategy decisions passed risk in all (the rest hit the 250-share position limit). The host's drain rate was not measured.

chokepoints.label: Core clock 250 MHz timing
chokepoints.peak_note: Measured on the xcu200 stand-in with the KR260 configuration after 9 timing fixes (docs/36): core -0.563 ns (was -2.957), xgmii +0.143 ns and host +1.551 ns met, hold met, every clock crossing passes. What remains is spread thinly across blocks. The K26 -2LV part (0.72 V, slower) is not installed in Vivado yet.

chokepoints.label: K26 block RAM
chokepoints.peak_note: Measured (docs/36): the 1-symbol KR260 build uses 28 RAMB36 (19%) and 48 of 64 URAM for the order store. 4 symbols take 112 RAMB36 but 110% of the K26's LUTs, so the build stays at 1 symbol.

chokepoints.label: Messages per µs (this window)
chokepoints.peak_note: Capacity = one message per 250 MHz cycle at best; C/D/E hold the book 18 cycles (~14/µs sustained). Busiest 1 µs in this window: 90 messages.

latency.t2t_def: first ITCH byte into itch_parser -> strategy decision_valid (latency_counter, tb_tick_to_trade, order_book_v3, 250 MHz)
latency.notes: Only measured numbers. mac_rx: first byte out ~3 XGMII words. strategy: the 70 ns parser->decision t2t (covers parser, kvs, book, strategy; risk adds 0). ouch: last ITCH byte -> whole 52-byte OUCH order, 60 ns (m2-book sim). PCS/PMA, CDC FIFOs, TCP and MAC tx not in this breakdown. Wire to wire on the KR260 path: 678 ns median with the 8-byte order path (1,280 ns byte-wide), 176 ns first ITCH byte -> risk-approved decision (docs/35, kr260-latency-test / widen-test).
